clue.text: Question archbishop entering into new negotiation

indicators.note: one piece going into another means it is placed inside it
something made new is remade, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
RR is Right Reverend, the style of a bishop, used loosely here for an archbishop

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is drawn into a fresh round of talks and starts asking questions.
explanation.walkthrough: Right Reverend strictly styles a bishop; the setter stretches it to an archbishop, who is a bishop too.
explanation.definitionFit: An interrogation is a formal questioning, so the noun question can stand for it.

clue.text: Incorrigible bishop tucks into hot dog and beer

indicators.note: one thing tucking into another is put inside it, so the bishop goes inside the drink

parts.note: in means fashionable, hot
a cur is a mongrel dog
ale is a type of beer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A hopeless bishop pigs out on a hot dog and a pint of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot dog' reads as one snack, but hot and dog are separate pieces; B goes inside ALE to make ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incurable cannot be put right, which is what incorrigible says of a person beyond reform.

clue.text: Gutless and stupid: The X-Factor must be sent up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: dim means slow-witted
'it' is the indefinable star quality also called the X factor

explanation.surface: A sneering verdict that the talent show The X Factor is cowardly and stupid and deserves mocking.
explanation.walkthrough: The X Factor is a British TV talent show, but here it means the quality called 'it'. DIM IT read upwards gives TIMID.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutless means lacking courage, and a timid person is shy and easily frightened.

clue.text: One captivated by wild or garden flower

indicators.note: being captivated, held captive, means sitting inside the other letters
wild suggests running out of control, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is enchanted by a flower, whether a wild one or one grown in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom but is the crossword sense of something that flows: a river. I sits after the first letter of the rearranged ORGARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is a river, and the Rio Grande runs between the United States and Mexico.

clue.text: Rotten cuts making daughter leave workplaces

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten

indicators.note: the daughter leaving means her abbreviation is taken out of the letters

parts.note: to dice is to cut into cubes
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Harsh budget cuts force a daughter to quit her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten cuts' reads as unfair cutbacks, but it is OFF DICES; removing the D leaves OFFICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Offices are rooms or buildings where people do their jobs, so they are workplaces.

clue.text: For villain, hero is one man Tony Montana holds

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, spread across its words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Tony Montana, the gangster of Scarface, is both villain and hero of his film.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sample sentence: hero is the opposite of villain.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, and hero is the opposite of villain.

clue.text: Children's publication

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one edition of a magazine or paper

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a children's magazine; the possessive hides two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring and also a single number of a periodical.

clue.text: Local angry about hotel just off The Strand?

parts.note: local means nearby

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hotel letter goes inside the word for angry

parts.note: sore means annoyed, angry
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A pub-goer is cross about a hotel located just off London's Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, but a strand is also a beach. H goes inside SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearshore describes waters close to the coast, just out from the beach or strand.

clue.text: Want marijuana if wife goes away for November

indicators.note: one letter going away for another means it is swapped out and the other takes its place

parts.note: weed is slang for marijuana
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone craves cannabis once their wife is away for the month of November.
explanation.walkthrough: November looks like a month but is the radio word for N, which replaces W in WEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to need it; both verbs mean to lack or require.

clue.text: How to stop sex addiction? Don't make me laugh!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: 'it' is slang for sex, and coming off something is giving it up
second meaning: an exclamation of disbelief

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at a question about curing sex addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a common euphemism for sex, so quitting it is coming off it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial retort telling someone to stop talking nonsense, like scornful disbelief.

clue.text: Bit of sudden worry could provide one

definitions.text: Bit of sudden worry could provide one

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of sudden
care means worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: A flash of unexpected anxiety is all it takes to give someone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a sudden worry is exactly what a fright is.
explanation.definitionFit: A scare is a sudden fright or alarm, so a burst of abrupt worry would bring one about.

clue.text: Free the Queen or Knight?

parts.note: to rid is to free from something
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A chess-style choice: release the Queen or the Knight?
explanation.walkthrough: Queen and Knight look like chess pieces; the question mark signals a knight as one example of a horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight traditionally fought on horseback, so he is an example of a horseman.

clue.text: Stupid dons conservative duke cut down to size?

indicators.note: putting something on in front, like a garment, means that piece is placed ahead of the other

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative
dense means slow-witted
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Dim university dons humble a Tory duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like academics but is the verb puts on, telling the conservative piece to go on in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A condensed text has been shortened or abridged, made smaller, which the question mark marks as a playful reading.

clue.text: After peeling off, they might give you slippers!

definitions.text: After peeling off, they might give you slippers!

parts.words: After peeling off, they might give you slippers!
parts.note: surface reading: once undressed, someone hands you house shoes

parts.words: After peeling off, they might give you slippers!
parts.note: setter's reading: the skins of a peeled fruit make people slip, so slippers are those who slip

explanation.walkthrough: Slippers sounds like footwear but means people who slip, on the classic discarded fruit skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel from this yellow fruit is the cartoon cause of pratfalls, so the peeled fruit leaves something slippery behind.

clue.text: Longs to open little drinks and chill

indicators.note: going in to open something means sitting inside it, between its first and later letters

parts.note: nips are small measures of spirits
to pine is to long for

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to crack open a few small drinks and relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chill' looks like the slang for relax, but it is the noun for coldness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippiness is sharp coldness in the air, as in a nippy morning, which is a chill.

clue.text: Huge insect chases old lady in Newcastle

indicators.note: one thing chasing another follows behind it, so it comes second

parts.note: mam is the Geordie word for mother, and old lady is slang for mother
a moth is a winged insect

explanation.surface: A giant bug pursues an elderly woman through Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle speech (Geordie) says mam for mum; 'old lady' is slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means enormous, from the huge extinct elephant.

clue.text: Temperamental car you and Den turned over

parts.note: Merc is short for a Mercedes car
U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for den is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A hot-headed driver complains that you and a friend called Den flipped the car.
explanation.walkthrough: Den has a capital to look like a name; LAIR backwards gives RIAL to end MERC U RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercurial means given to sudden mood swings, like quicksilver, which is temperamental.

clue.text: A theorist vacillating could be one

definitions.text: A theorist vacillating could be one

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering to and fro, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker who keeps wavering between ideas is a ditherer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a theorist who cannot make up their mind is exactly someone who wavers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hesitator is one who pauses and wavers, and an undecided thinker is just that.

clue.text: English leader must avoid strike in Victoria?

indicators.note: the leading letter must keep away, and English takes its place

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
to impress is to stamp or strike a mark into something

explanation.surface: A head of state in the Australian state of Victoria must steer clear of industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English leader' looks like a prime minister; really E replaces the first letter of IMPRESS. Queen Victoria was also Empress of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria held the title Empress of India, so she is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: High point of church: having hour for time with the flock!

indicators.note: having one thing for another means a swap, so one letter is exchanged for a different one

parts.note: a steeple is the tall spire of a church
T is the abbreviation for time
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: The church spire looms over the congregation, the shepherd's flock.
explanation.walkthrough: The flock looks like a congregation; it means people who follow the crowd like sheep. H replaces T in STEEPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheeple is a scornful word for docile people who conform like a flock of sheep.

clue.text: Shows on the telly with vets

explanation.surface: Television programmes featuring animal doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: Vets looks like animal doctors but is the verb meaning checks.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is both to broadcast on television and to examine candidates thoroughly.

clue.text: Retrospective work covering REM and The Boss?

indicators.note: covering means surrounding, so the band name sits inside
retrospective means looking back, so the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
the band name taken as written

explanation.surface: A career retrospective of rock music featuring R.E.M. and Bruce Springsteen, nicknamed The Boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boss is Springsteen's nickname, but here it simply means a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, informally a boss or head.

clue.text: I hear he plays in winning group of players

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for winning

parts.note: up means ahead, winning, as in two goals up

indicators.note: the words play about, rearranging themselves into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a certain player turns out for the champion team.
explanation.walkthrough: Players look like a sports team; Uriah Heep is a British rock band, named after the Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is a long-running hard rock band, a group of musicians or players.

clue.text: One question asked of needle-user in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it is heard spoken rather than how it is written

parts.note: you would ask someone holding knitting needles whether they knit

explanation.surface: Someone asks a knitter a question about their craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The needle-user looks like a nurse or addict; it is a knitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing or the number one, so it can stand for one.

clue.text: I say the inferno's nonexistent

parts.note: hell is the inferno of damnation
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone declares that hell does not exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like the start of a statement but is the definition: an exclamation of greeting or surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections used to attract attention or express surprise, so the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Disturb group of people in the best of moods?

parts.note: up means cheerful, in high spirits
a set is a group or circle of people

explanation.surface: Spoiling the mood of a cheerful crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to disturb their composure or trouble them.

clue.text: Way to embrace little darling

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, wrapping around something, so it goes inside

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
wee is Scots for little

explanation.surface: A tender way to cuddle a little loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: Darling here is the adjective, as in a darling little cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Darling as an adjective means charming or lovely, which is sweet.

clue.text: I possibly sell horse (the best one can get)

parts.note: taken as written
horse is slang for heroin, and to deal is to sell drugs

explanation.surface: A trader offers a horse for sale, which they say is the best there is.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse looks like the animal but is drug slang for heroin; selling drugs is dealing, so 'I possibly sell horse' is I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal is the perfect example, the most excellent thing achievable.

clue.text: Ultimately crap citizen: Trump, perhaps

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the closing letter of crap
a resident is someone who lives in a place, a citizen

explanation.surface: A scathing jab calling Donald Trump a lousy citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an insult, but crap just yields its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump has served as President of the United States, so he is an example, as perhaps signals.

clue.text: Inevitably, blasted ale leads to omissions, negligence and to errors

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so all the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leads to means the leading, opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: the opening letter of omissions
the opening letter of negligence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinking too much beer will eventually cause slips, carelessness and mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the opening letters of omissions and negligence join the beer and the closing phrase in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens at some point, whatever the timing, is bound to happen: inevitably.
